title: [17.0.0-rc.0] migrate CLI and dev runtime disagree on __search companion provisioning — migrate flags live search columns as destructive orphans
body:
Found during the HotCRM 17.0.0-rc.0 upgrade (tag commit `fc156fa4a`). Reproducible column-level evidence below.

## Symptom
`os migrate plan` against a database created by `objectstack dev` reports 9 destructive `drop_column` ops for `__search` companion columns (crm_task, crm_competitor, crm_opportunity_line_item, crm_quote_line_item, sys_metadata, sys_metadata_history, sys_metadata_commit, sys_metadata_audit, sys_view_definition):

> `crm_task.__search: column exists in the database but not in metadata (orphaned) — "os migrate apply --allow-destructive" to drop it.`

## Evidence — the two boot paths build different schemas from the same source tree
Same worktree, same artifact, two fresh databases:

| | created by | crm_task columns | `__search` present |
|---|---|---|---|
| dev.db | `objectstack dev` first boot | 34 | **yes** |
| probe-fresh.db | `os migrate plan --database-url file:...` (CLI boot DDL) | 33 | **no** |

And `os migrate plan` against its **own** freshly created DB reports 0 destructive changes — i.e. the "orphans" appear exactly when the DB was born under the dev runtime and judged by the CLI.

## Why this is worse than a cosmetic warning
- The columns are not orphans: they are the search-companion columns (`provisionSearchCompanion` / plugin-pinyin-search) the dev runtime provisions and maintains. Following the CLI's own remediation advice (`--allow-destructive`) deletes live feature columns; the next dev boot presumably re-provisions them — churn at best, broken search at worst.
- Every dev-created SQLite database permanently nags with 9 destructive ops, training operators to reach for `--allow-destructive`.

## Likely shape of the defect
The CLI boot (`packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts` → runtime.start → syncRegisteredSchemas) either doesn't load the search plugin or computes companion eligibility differently from the dev runtime, so the metadata it diffs against lacks the `__search` fields for those 9 objects. Whichever side is "right", create/serve and plan/apply must share one schema view.

## Related minor asymmetry (same family)
A brand-new CLI-created DB *immediately* reports the 3 "safe" `replace_unique_index` relaxations from #3696 (`uniq_crm_contact_email` → `(organization_id, email)` etc.) — i.e. the create path still emits the legacy platform-wide unique indexes that drift immediately wants to replace. The #3696 fix appears to have updated drift but not table creation.
